analysis:
Changed behavior is in EngineV2Factory+BackendPreparation.swift, head lines 180-183 and 224-228. FlintModel with kvBackend == .auto is now treated as explicit .paged, which skips the automatic crash-loop guard at line 215. The guard is bypassed only for that model type. A new refusal at line 224 throws pagedUnavailable if Flint resolves to anything other than paged, for example through the model_capability or kill_switch veto. Later paged failures also refuse rather than degrade, because degradesPagedFailure(selection: .paged) is expected to refuse. That function's implementation was not supplied, so this is inferred from the existing comment at line 210/214 and the existing degradeOrRefuse comment.

Security impact: this is fail-closed for one model type and adds no new data exposure. It does not touch encryption, the SSD prefix cache (T-041), attestation, authorization or the coordinator trust boundary. Availability can degrade for Flint when paged is vetoed or fails, because the load is refused instead of served on contiguous. That is an intentional qualification choice, not an attacker-controlled path. The environment kill switch is operator-controlled, which is within ADV-001's own machine and affects only that operator's availability.

The test file changes are benchmark dispatch tests only (usesNativeGeneration and measuresScalarPrefill for flint) and carry no production security effect. I did not see the production implementations of ModelBenchmark or ThroughputSweep, so I cannot confirm they match the tests.

Open integration questions: whether EngineV2KVBackendPolicy.degradesPagedFailure returns false for .paged, and whether Flint paged precision (the EngineV2KVQuantizationPolicy.resolve flint path) interacts with the prefix cache. Neither was supplied. No finding qualifies.
